answer: Before trading, each agent earns an epoch work ticket from a puzzle seeded by its public key, so one solution cannot serve two identities. It runs 4 hours on a $1.20-per-hour GPU; the registrar checks the hash in 1 second, and a late proof fails closed. That ticket is one thread in its audit trail; 1,000 Sybils cost 1,000 x $4.80 = $4,800 per epoch, versus $4.80 honest. At dawn each epoch the seed rotates, so attackers cannot stockpile a reef of pre-solved identities for a flood. Like a harbour admitting only boats that burned fuel, it admits only agents that spent compute.
